author: Adeel Ahmad
title: Systems, AI & Security
intro: I'm a software engineer in Melbourne. This page is for people who have my CV and want to understand how the different parts of it connect.
description: A dated record of what Adeel Ahmad worked on and learned, across software, infrastructure, security and AI.

events.title: Getting into security
events.body: I started poking at networks and security in grade 8 in Lahore, long before my first software job.

events.title: First formal vulnerability assessment
events.body: In 2006, while still at school, I did my first formal vulnerability assessment, on a company's website, and found issues that would have let attackers in. The company's CEO later wrote me a recommendation letter.

events.title: Computer-science education
events.body: Studied computer science at the Institute of Management Sciences in Lahore while working.

events.title: APTLOGIX: application development and integration
events.body: My first professional role included CMS and e-commerce development, C#/.NET backends and third-party integrations.

events.title: Senior Software Engineer at PureLogics
events.body: Worked as a senior software engineer before taking on a wider technical role.

events.title: PureLogics: co-partner and CTO
events.body: Kept developing while also looking after network security and the company's systems.

events.title: Virtualization, networks and telephony
events.body: Worked with VMware, Asterisk and Cisco networking. Later I moved from VMware to XenServer, and then to Proxmox/KVM.
events.note: I don’t have exact start dates for these.

events.title: A Facebook-integrated application
events.body: Worked on a community application that integrated with Facebook's APIs.

events.title: Enterprise workflow automation
events.body: Built tools to automate quality-assurance workflows for a business.

events.title: Co-founded Geeks Chicago
events.body: Co-founded a small consultancy and worked on client projects and solution design.

events.title: Xoho Tech: founder and CTO
events.body: Ran a consultancy that grew to about 40 people across Pakistan and the United States. I wrote code, designed systems, handled security and delivery, and did the sales.

events.title: Starting with AWS
events.body: AWS became part of our client work early on.

events.title: Digital archives and video platforms
events.body: Worked on AWS-hosted archive and video-streaming systems with searchable collections.

events.title: Archive management
events.body: Built archive-management and audiovisual systems: data models, media handling and search.

events.title: Tools for archival quality and integrity
events.body: Worked on several applications for managing archive collections and checking data quality and file integrity.

events.title: An e-signature application
events.body: Worked on an e-signature application on AWS: the signing workflows and integration with other business systems.

events.title: Writing down our engineering practices
events.body: Wrote the company's engineering guide: cloud practices, identity, secure coding, style and onboarding.

events.title: AWS Solutions Architect Associate
events.body: My first AWS certification.

events.title: Power cuts became a developer problem
events.body: Power cuts kept interrupting work and sometimes losing it. I started looking at hosting development environments remotely so work would survive an outage.

events.title: Taking the browser IDE apart
events.body: Looked at how VS Code separates the editor, the extension host and background services, then used browser-hosted VS Code in our later remote workspaces.

events.title: A home lab to learn the layers underneath
events.body: Built a small Proxmox, Ceph and ZFS cluster at home to understand storage and virtualisation properly.

events.title: Shared, template-based development environments
events.body: Built Linux-container templates with project dependencies and browser-based editing on a rented European server. Private networking, cloning and shared resources made the environment reusable across developers.

events.title: Stopping idle workspaces
events.body: Used a web server and shell scripts to stop idle workspaces and start them again when a browser request came in, instead of keeping every environment running.

events.title: Firecracker developer environments
events.body: Moved the workspace experiments from containers toward Firecracker microVMs, weighing isolation against resource use and startup time.

events.title: Teaching the team containers
events.body: Taught the team containers and some of the infrastructure under our applications.

events.title: Workspaces for onboarding and handovers
events.body: Used saved editor state, snapshots, cloneable environments and preinstalled dependencies so people could hand over work, get started on a project, or come back to an old one.

events.title: Media-monitoring platform work
events.body: Worked on systems that collect, search and monitor media content.

events.title: Planning an open platform for audiovisual metadata
events.body: I was on the core team planning an open platform that uses speech recognition, OCR and other machine learning to describe large audiovisual archives. In September 2017 we spent three days on requirements, comparing candidate tools for each part of the pipeline and sketching workflows. The plan was presented at the AMIA conference that December.
events.evidence: Workshop notes, September 2017, and public project documentation

events.title: Access to OpenAI's API beta
events.body: Got access to OpenAI's private API beta while running the consultancy, and started experimenting with it.
events.note: This is the date access was granted.

events.title: Researching browser-based compute and developer tooling
events.body: Explored browser extensions, React internals, WebRTC desktop access, cloud isolation and customizable developer environments.

events.title: Cevo: AWS cloud consulting
events.body: Moved into cloud consulting in Australia, working across solution architecture, application integration and technical delivery.

events.title: Cloud API delivery and domain-team leadership
events.body: Built cloud APIs and integrations, including Consumer Data Right services, and led the engineers working on them.

events.title: Enterprise search that respects permissions
events.body: Worked on enterprise search with Amazon Q Business and SharePoint, where results had to respect who is allowed to see each document.

events.title: Document and email processing pipelines
events.body: Worked on pipelines that process documents and email, using dbt, machine learning and Amazon Bedrock.

events.title: WebRTC beyond the browser IDE
events.body: Tried streaming full desktops to the browser over WebRTC, for development and QA work that needed more than an editor and a shell. Looked at bandwidth, frame rate, audio and what the client device needed.

events.title: Explaining LLMs and Transformers
events.body: Prepared presentation material on Transformers, attention, fine-tuning, prompts, agents and plugins.

events.title: Writing about open language models
events.body: Wrote about open models like Falcon, which can be adapted and run outside a single vendor’s service.

events.title: The development environment is part of DevOps
events.body: Wrote up the idea that development environments should be versioned and reproducible like any other build, with dependencies, prebuilds and tooling defined in the delivery process instead of a setup guide.

events.title: Separate the IDE from the application runtime
events.body: Sketched a workspace with separate containers for the editor and the application, possibly run on ECS or EKS.

events.title: Built workspace images with GitLab CI/CD
events.body: Adapted an existing workspace base image, added project dependencies in a Dockerfile and arranged automated environment builds on change.

events.title: Developer portals as a shared starting point
events.body: Proposed an internal developer portal for APIs, docs, examples and environment setup. Backstage was one option I looked at.

events.title: Extension licensing as a design constraint
events.body: Checked how custom IDE builds, extension marketplaces and their licence terms would affect the developer-platform design.

events.title: Keeping workspaces near shared services
events.body: Looked at keeping development close to shared services, controlling package access in one place, and keeping the workspace separate from the device a developer uses to reach it.

events.title: Private AI coding assistance
events.body: Proposed connecting privately hosted models to the development environments, so code stayed private and people had less reason to use unapproved AI tools.

events.title: AI preparing a Jira task before a developer starts
events.body: Sketched a workflow where a new Jira task starts a temporary development environment, and an AI prepares a plan and a first pass before the engineer takes over.
events.note: This was a proposal. It wasn't built as a whole.

events.title: Showing the plan and checking the result
events.body: In the same design, the engineer could see what the AI planned and what it actually did, check the work, and stayed responsible for the result.

events.title: Runnable environments for pull-request review
events.body: Proposed opening each pull request in a running browser workspace, so a reviewer could try the change as well as read the code.

events.title: Starting with a small pilot
events.body: Worked out what the developer platform would cost to run and to teach, and suggested a small pilot with runnable examples instead of building everything at once.

events.title: A talk on our remote-development setup
events.body: Gave a talk on how our setup went from hosted workspaces to containers, prebuilt environments and AI-assisted workflows.

events.title: Small, domain-specific models on consumer hardware
events.body: Shared experiments fine-tuning small GPT-NeoX models for one task, such as drafting email, and running them on ordinary hardware.

events.title: Article-to-podcast workflow in Python
events.body: Wrote a Python script that rewrites an article as a podcast script and reads it out with macOS text-to-speech.

events.title: Browser-to-podcast automation with Shortcuts
events.body: Shared an iOS/macOS Shortcut that does the same from the browser, without a terminal.

events.title: Thinking about small-model serving economics
events.body: Wrote about serving small models that sit idle most of the time, and what it costs to keep a model loaded in memory.

events.title: Local and edge AI as an architectural choice
events.body: Wrote about running smaller models closer to the data, for privacy and cost reasons.

events.title: A multi-agent AutoGen prototype
events.body: Built a GPT-4 and AutoGen notebook with roles such as account manager, architect, critic and engineer, with a person approving the plan before code ran.

events.title: Knowledge graphs, vector search and RAG together
events.body: Argued that graph structure and vector search work better together than vector search alone.

events.title: Prompt and SQL-injection risks in AI applications
events.body: Pointed out injection risks in an approach that let a model query data, especially where untrusted input reaches templates and tools.

events.title: Private, multi-model agent orchestration
events.body: Wrote about AutoGen and Griptape as ways to combine several models in one agent system, including private or open models.

events.title: Using language models in honeypots
events.body: Suggested using language models to make honeypots more convincing and more useful for studying attackers.

events.title: Structured metadata for retrieval
events.body: Wrote about how RDF and structured metadata can help language models find the right information.

events.title: Public talk: a generative AI second brain on AWS serverless
events.body: Gave a talk on building a personal "second brain" on AWS serverless while keeping the cost low. Most of it does not need a large model or real-time answers, so documents are stored in S3, organised with small keyword and topic models, and searched with a vector database that sits on S3. Small quantized models handle the cheap steps, and retrieval with a larger model runs only for content I pick.

events.title: Local supervised fine-tuning
events.body: Fine-tuned Llama and OpenChat-class models locally with llama.cpp: preparing the training data, training, and checking the results.

events.title: Synthetic data, fine-tuning and quantization loops
events.body: Tried a loop where a model helps write and clean up training data for one task, then gets fine-tuned and quantized, and the cycle repeats.

events.title: Writing up AI-prepared developer workspaces
events.body: Wrote up the 2023 idea publicly: once requirements and Jira tasks exist, a model plans and prepares the work in an isolated environment, and the engineer still owns and reviews the code.

events.title: Personal assistants and audio knowledge workflows
events.body: Wrote about personal-assistant workflows built from open tools and automation that turn reading material into short written or audio briefings.

events.title: Structured reasoning with smaller models
events.body: Tried the situation, task, action, result (STAR) structure to guide small quantized models through a task and a review of their own work.

events.title: Training data with explicit reasoning and protection structure
events.body: Tried building fine-tuning data that spells out the reasoning steps, including steps meant to resist misuse.

events.title: Models and serialized data
events.body: Asked how models behave when given serialized or binary data, and what security risks that opens.

events.title: Trying Cedar for policy-as-code
events.body: Wrote about experiments with Cedar and how hard it is to manage security policy at scale.

events.title: Small models in serverless functions
events.body: Wrote about using ONNX to fit small-model inference into serverless functions such as Lambda.

events.title: AI platform security is not application security
events.body: Wrote about the security gaps that stay in the application even when the AI platform underneath has good controls.

events.title: AWS Solutions Architect Professional
events.body: Passed the AWS Solutions Architect Professional exam.

events.title: Snowflake SnowPro Core
events.body: Passed the SnowPro Core exam while working on data platforms.

events.title: Lyrebird Health: tech lead on a clinical AI product
events.body: Tech lead on a clinical AI product, covering the AWS setup, AI engineering and security.

events.title: Clinical AI: evaluation and traceability
events.body: On the clinical product I worked on structured extraction, evaluation (including LLM-as-judge), prompt versioning, tracing each statement back to its source, and protecting sensitive data.

events.title: Early voice-AI evaluation
events.body: Took part in early testing of a voice AI product, which got me into realtime and streaming systems.

events.title: Responsible-disclosure work in AI systems
events.body: Worked on AI-system security research and submitted a vulnerability report through a responsible-disclosure channel.

events.title: Prompt experiments with reasoning models
events.body: Shared what I noticed when testing reward-style wording in prompts for reasoning models.

events.title: Commonwealth Bank: Staff Platform Engineer
events.body: Joined Commonwealth Bank’s AI Acceleration squad.

events.title: Taking AI applications to production
events.body: Work across development, data and infrastructure to take AI applications from early design into production.

events.title: Identity and authorization for AI applications
events.body: Worked on identity and authorization between services, and between agents and their tools, using least privilege and avoiding shared secrets.

events.title: Researching small-model reasoning with RL and SFT
events.body: Wrote publicly about using reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning to study reasoning in small models.

events.title: Security testing of AI applications
events.body: Tested AI applications for security problems, mainly where model output turns into application behaviour.

events.title: Comparing audio-analysis approaches
events.body: Built a Gradio prototype to compare ways of analysing audio: telling speakers apart, timestamps, and interacting with what was said.

events.title: Writing about capability and agent risk
events.body: Wrote about the security risks that come with more capable models and agents, and the trade-offs of using smaller, task-specific models.

events.title: An AI hackathon team
events.body: Led a team at an internal AI hackathon, from the problem to a working demo.

events.title: Mentoring, standards and engineering delivery
events.body: Besides hands-on engineering, I help with design discussions, mentor engineers and work on how the team delivers.

events.title: Security Champion
events.body: Took on the Security Champion role for my squad.

events.title: Declarative agents and filesystem-native tools
events.body: Suggested defining agents declaratively and exposing their tools as ordinary files and command-line programs.

events.title: Reasoning scaffolds for small models
events.body: Studied how small models learn when given reasoning scaffolds, and compared the insides of base and fine-tuned models.

events.title: Testing what model adaptation preserves and changes
events.body: Shared what I saw inside models after fine-tuning, and suggested checking whether it holds for other model families.

events.title: Latent Contextual Reinforcement
events.body: Wrote up a research idea about guiding small models to reason better without retraining all of their weights.

events.title: A Go proxy for models and tools
events.body: A single Go binary that offers an OpenAI-style chat API, routes to different model backends, and keeps tool registration and execution separate.

events.title: JuiceFS fork: storage, caching and backend engineering
events.body: Working in a JuiceFS fork on storage backends, caching, replication, integrity and block access.
events.note: This is work in my fork, not an upstream JuiceFS release.

events.title: MLX model-inspection and comparison tools
events.body: Built command-line tools that show a model’s predictions layer by layer, compare activations between models, measure drift and run ablations.

events.title: A lesson in parallel-agent integration
events.body: Running several coding agents in parallel, I let them build on a shared interface before it was settled, and had to redo work. Now I agree on and test the shared interface first.

events.title: CTXConfig: choose context at the symbol level
events.body: Tried choosing context for coding agents by symbol, using the syntax tree, instead of feeding in whole files.

events.title: agentic-agile: test-driven agent workflows
events.body: Published a Claude Code plugin where I approve the plan first, tests come before code, work goes through review, and a task is only done when its checks pass.

events.title: Measuring agent-assisted development
events.body: Reported the numbers from one agent-assisted development run (tokens, packages, tests, commits) instead of just saying it worked.

events.title: Running agents in microVMs
events.body: Ran packaged agents in microVMs with libkrun and compared isolation options against the same list of requirements.

events.title: AgentRC: writing down what an agent may do
events.body: Published a draft spec: a packaged agent lists the models, tools and network access it needs, and the platform can allow, narrow or refuse each one before it runs.

events.title: Looking back at local-model work
events.body: Wrote a look back from early fastText and local-model work to later fine-tuning and defensive tool design.

events.title: rclone filesystem adapters and media integration
events.body: Built filesystem adapters in an rclone fork, including one for a media server. The upstream proposal was closed without merging.

events.title: Versioned work state, not just conversation history
events.body: Designed a state document that records decisions, versions and task status across agent sessions, with an interactive view of how it changed over time.

events.title: Keeping my AI conversations
events.body: Built browser extensions to save my own AI conversations, and what they produced, as files I keep.

events.title: Local Python execution inside a document editor
events.body: Prototyped a browser extension that runs Python locally with Pyodide, so code examples in a document can run where they are written.

events.title: MLX reinforcement-learning and guided-training tooling
events.body: Developed training tooling for Apple Silicon, with configurable tasks, evaluators, rewards, supervised modes and guided reasoning experiments.

events.title: OpenWrt traffic-control fix merged upstream
events.body: Fixed bidirectional traffic shaping in luci-app-trafficctl, with tests. The pull request was merged upstream.

events.title: Out-of-band automation through PiKVM
events.body: Prototyped a hardware-control interface for fixing and administering machines when the normal network is down.

events.title: Local GRPO and LoRA experiments on Apple Silicon
events.body: Kept training small models at home: guided-reasoning runs, quantisation and tooling to make runs repeatable.

events.title: ReqWall: request rules kept separate from enforcement
events.body: Tried keeping request-blocking rules in one place, so whatever enforces them, the browser or the router, can be swapped.

events.title: A media-ingestion pipeline
events.body: Started a reusable pipeline that takes in audio, video and images and makes them searchable.

events.title: Android device management
events.body: Checked what Android device management is actually possible, and made ADB and Shizuku start reliably.

events.title: agent-handoff: durable decisions across sessions
events.body: Published a Go tool that carries settled decisions, open tasks and versioned state from one AI session to the next, so I don’t rebuild context each time.

events.title: Snapback: browse backup history without replacing live data
events.body: Designed a Linux/macOS tool to browse backup history read-only, folder by folder, and copy files back, without ever mounting over the live files.

events.title: aloop: the next version of agentic-agile
events.body: Reworked agentic-agile into aloop: test-driven agents, rounds of review, a final check, and a handoff file carried between fresh sessions.

events.title: Workstation recovery and GPU diagnostics
events.body: Worked through memory compatibility, firmware settings, storage and network hardware, Linux drivers and GPU recovery on an older workstation.

events.title: Browser storage and extension debugging
events.body: Exported data from IndexedDB and worked out why DOM and URL APIs behaved differently in page, extension and worker contexts.

events.title: Wireless backhaul and OpenWrt diagnostics
events.body: Investigated home wireless-backhaul constraints, routing and bridging behavior, TCP settings and radio state across a mixed-device network.

events.title: A writing project on AI application principles
events.body: Began shaping a writing project about repeatable architecture, governance and operating principles for AI applications.

events.title: USB-device emulation on Raspberry Pi
events.body: Started a USB device-emulation prototype on a Raspberry Pi Zero, possibly moving to other hardware later.

events.title: Privacy questions in voice-AI pipelines
events.body: Looked at how voice-AI pipelines handle personal information in streaming audio and voice tokens.

events.title: anytopdf: media to searchable documents
events.body: Designed a pipeline that turns files, images, audio and video into searchable documents, with transcripts, captions and keyframe notes. The first version is in Python; a later one may move to Rust.

events.title: Lens: look and interface
events.body: Worked on the look and interface for Lens across web, app and command line.

events.title: Lens: a private AI hub
events.body: Planned a private AI hub that runs on my own machines: my notes and files, searchable, with answers that cite sources and actions that need my approval.

events.title: Putting this record together
events.body: Put this timeline together to show how the work connects.

events.title: Security research at execution boundaries
events.body: Studied the sandbox boundaries of AI execution environments through protocol and systems analysis. Unpublished findings are not listed here.

events.title: Speech recognition, OCR and visual-media processing
events.body: Worked with speech-recognition, OCR and media-processing tools before the later LLM-focused projects.

events.title: Telephony and realtime communication
events.body: Worked across Asterisk, FreePBX and later telephony systems, including audio codecs, recording, SMS integration and realtime browser communication.

events.title: Routing, VPNs and identity-aware access
events.body: Worked with switching, routing, firewalls, overlay networks, VPNs and identity-aware access, picked up over many years and projects.

events.title: MacPilot: natural-language desktop automation
events.body: Experimented with model-driven macOS control using accessibility interfaces, AppleScript, OCR and asynchronous orchestration.

method.scope: This is a selection, not everything. Work for employers and clients is described in general terms, without client names or internal details.
method.evidence: Some entries link to public posts or code. The rest come from my own notes and records.
method.dates: Some dates are exact and some are approximate. Approximate ones say so.
method.skills: Skill tags show what a piece of work involved. They are not ratings.
method.research: Experiments and proposals are labelled as such. Not everything here was finished or went into production.
